# idea-0004: A UI for the estate
========================================================================

status: active · appetite: 3 · created: 2026-08-28 · state-head: state/0009.md · seed: exports/0004-estate-ui-seed.md
relates (note, not an edge): idea-0001 is the natural candidate; `relate` is The Cartographer's, and it has not run

## Artifacts — the agents' track

### 0001 · Spark · "A UI for the estate"
capture · The Gardener · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [] · challenged: false
T wants a UI for the estate itself — a visual map of how an idea travels, with clean jumps between projects and the ideas/sub-ideas within — arriving alongside a fresh glossary that already flags two of its words as things the repo does not yet have.

### 0002 · Framing · "The record is complete; the view of it is missing"
frame · The Gardener · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0001] · challenged: false
The estate's record is complete but illegible at a glance — every fact a map needs is in frontmatter, yet the file tree renders storage rather than travel, and T, a visual learner, cannot see the thing that has been built. The framing takes the map before the tree (the lineage graph is derivable today; the hierarchy T's words name is not), takes read-only before dispatch (a surface that writes or steers collides with the writer seam and the unaddressable steering layer), and takes in-repo static as the home (self-containment is law). The tension: the honest map can show every place an idea stopped and nothing of what steered it between stops — and this record must not become the pressure that fixes that, because that ground belongs to idea-0001.

### 0003 · Horizon · "The estate, visible"
envision · The Architect · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0002] · challenged: false · horizon: falsifiable
The viewer, working, is one self-contained HTML file in the repo that T opens with one command and that renders the estate as travel instead of storage: a portfolio shelf that answers 'where is everything and what moved' in five seconds, and per-record maps that lay the artifact lineage graph against the Steward's state track with the steering gap drawn as a visible labeled seam. The architectural call left open by the Framing is made here: build-time-generated, not runtime-parsed — file:// blocks fetch in every mainstream browser, so runtime parsing forces a local server, whereas generation makes the viewer a member of a category the estate already owns (derived data, like SURVEY.md, with a covers: staleness stamp), and the regenerate step collapses into the open command itself. Feature inventory tiered honestly: everything on the map is drawable from frontmatter that exists today; the cheap unlocks are named (run survey once, run relate once, place three binaries); every refusal carries its wall (third writer, steering surface, unapproved schema). Falsifiable four ways, including one this Horizon adds: if the staleness banner is what T sees on most opens, the build-time call was the wrong half of the deferred decision.

### 0004 · Trajectory · "The route to the viewer"
chart · The Surveyor · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0003] · challenged: false · trajectory: actionable
Five legs, sized for afternoons and weekends, ordered by the Horizon's own constraints: the generator's graph derivation first, proven as plain text against idea-0003 before a pixel exists; the shelf second, because it is the smaller surface and the one falsifier 1 measures; the record map third; the reading panel and clean jump fourth; and a fifth leg that is not a build at all but the scheduled reading of the falsifiers. The route is deliberately truncatable: after leg 2 T has an openable viewer on real data, after leg 3 the map T actually asked for — a low appetite cuts the tail, not the trunk. Opening honesty first: appetite on this record is still the placeholder 1, so this route is sized to heat T has never set, and it says so before it says anything else. First actionable step: on any Saturday, write the zero-dependency generator and make it print idea-0003's branch, fan-out, and backward provenance line as text.

### 0005 · Phase · "Phase 1 — The parser and the proof"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0004] · challenged: false
Delivers the generator's spine with no pixels: a zero-dependency Node script at docs/estate-view/generate.mjs that walks ideas/ and exports/, parses the frontmatter subset in use, derives the full graph, and prints it as plain text — proven against a written list of idea-0003 fixture assertions (the 0008→0009 branch with 0009 tip, the 0010→0011 chain caught by the same rule, the seven-way fan-out from 0012, the Seed's nine inbound edges and one backward provenance line, thirteen states with their rungs). Waits on nothing; startable this Saturday; cost one Saturday. The checkpoint is the assertion list itself, and it is where Framing assumption 4 bites: if the graph cannot be derived from frontmatter alone, gaps render as gaps — and if the record is too broken to draw at all, the re-route is back to T with the specific missing links named, never to repair-by-inference.

### 0006 · Phase · "Phase 2 — The shelf and the open command"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0004] · challenged: false

Triggered by Phase 1's assertions going green; cost one weekend. ### 0007 · Phase · "Phase 3 — The travel map"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0004] · challenged: false
Delivers the per-record travel map — the thing T actually asked for: the state rail on the left with session-verbs, the artifact field on the right in the ten-type domain-neutral glyph vocabulary, version chains stacked tip-bright over dimmed superseded versions, the seven-way fan-out fanned, the Seed outside the record's wall with nine edges gathering through it and the single backward provenance line drawn distinctly, rungs tying rail to field, the uniform hatched steering seam between every pair of states carrying its full label, and the assets strip reading MANIFEST statuses. Domain-generality (falsifier 4) is armed here: glyphs come from the type table and nothing else.

### 0008 · Phase · "Phase 4 — The reading panel and the clean jump"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0004] · challenged: false

The vocabulary contract (Framing assumption 5) bites hardest here, in every label and every synonym: canon into UI, never UI into canon.

### 0010 · Horizon · "The estate, visible — and then the estate, shared"
explore · The Forager · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0003] · challenged: false · horizon: falsifiable
This record now holds two horizons and a seam drawn Starvu-style between them: the near horizon is the local viewer exactly as the sealed Seed exports it — unchanged here, standing alone, nothing in it a stub for anything later — and the far horizon is T's platform vision, stated 2026-08-28: the estate as a multi-user product with database-backed records, login and per-user ownership, the lineage map as the main window, and an in-window AI chat that is the Steward through conversation, not a chatbox. The seam constraint is the Starvu house rule: no login stubs, no disabled chat pane, no 'coming soon' in the viewer; what genuinely transfers is named (the Phase-1 graph derivation as the platform's core algorithm, the two-rail visual language, the glossary as label contract, honest-empty-states and classify-never-gate as product DNA) and what does not is named too (file parsing, the regenerate-and-open command, the committed index.html). Two findings the fold surfaced: T's own report of confusion is the Framing's read-hostile claim confirmed by its primary source, strengthening the near horizon independently; and a database platform makes idea-0001's unaddressable steering layer addressable by construction — packets become rows — which is where F5's pressure route may land. The five falsifiers carry unchanged; three far-horizon falsifiers are added, honestly marked as named-but-unarmed until the platform has a first decision point.

### 0014 · Trajectory · "The road in two versions"

V1 refuses every stub the seam law forbids (the Access gate passes because it is zero code and right for v1 alone); v2 waits on a decided and used v1, which is F6's reading. First actionable step: next session, dispatch the two owed decides — the exposure decision unblocks the gate the same day. Steps carry human-attention tags per T's standing convention of 2026-08-28: every leg is evaluated for whether an agent can perform the work itself, and **[HUMAN ATTENTION]** marks the six of twelve (v1.1, v1.2, v1.6; v2.2, v2.5, v2.6) where it cannot — account consent, purchases, the content of T's own judgment, and lived use — while the silent remainder asserts the work is AI-performable. Needing T's approval is not needing T's hands; the tag marks only the latter.

# idea-0001: The Estate
========================================================================

status: active · appetite: 3 · created: 2026-08-25 · state-head: state/0011.md

## Artifacts — the agents' track

### 0001 · Spark · "First full arc — residue"
capture · The Gardener · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [] · challenged: false
Nine observations about how the estate itself functioned during idea-0003's first full arc — dispatch substitution, the chat channel carrying load, unrouted binaries, and other residue that belongs on this record, not that one.

### 0002 · Spark · "First full arc — residue, challenged"
challenge · The Advocate · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0001] · challenged: true
The residue is a largely accurate but self-selected report: five items hold, three bend, one breaks — and of the two syntheses layered on it, the 'one unguarded door' is three-quarters true and the Steward's 'it functioned' verdict fails the estate's own falsifiability standard outright. Four omissions added, the largest being that the dispatch packets themselves — the channel that shapes every agent's work — exist nowhere on the record.

### 0003 · Framing · "The estate's steering is not one of its citizens"
frame · The Gardener · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [0002] · challenged: false
The ground is that the estate's provenance machinery — typing, lineage, classifiers, immutability, verb-addressability — reaches only what verbs produce, while the acts that decide which verb runs, on what, and with what framing are by construction not produced by verbs. The unrecorded-channel cluster is the inbound half of that same population and the unexamined-hub asymmetry is its internal half; the classifier-consequence question is largely a separate, smaller defect and is parked rather than absorbed. The tension is that the writer seam, which is the law that creates the blind spot, is also the law that makes the record trustworthy.

### 0004 · Spark · "Second day — residue"
capture · The Gardener · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [] · challenged: false
Eight residue items from the estate's second working day: fast-track improvised without a home in law, a two-verb dispatch with one snapshot, the unguarded door guarded by habit, operator confusion entering the record as falsifier data, a fixture going stale inside a single session, Steward-authored documentation outside the writer seam, a sealed Seed held against an exciting pivot, and a reversed assumption leaving the sealed export stale.

### 0005 · Decision · "The human-attention tag"
decide · The Chancellor · 2026-08-28 · inputs: [] · challenged: false
T decided, and this Decision seals, that every step in every roadmap artifact — Trajectory legs and Phase steps alike — is evaluated for whether a human must perform it, that steps an AI agent definitely cannot perform carry the inline marker **[HUMAN ATTENTION]**, and that absence of the marker is itself an assertion that the work is AI-performable. The load-bearing distinction, and the reason the tag carries information at all, is that needing T's approval is not the same as needing T's hands: this estate already requires T's approval for everything, so a tag keyed to approval would mark every step and discriminate nothing — the tag marks work an agent cannot do no matter how freely approval is granted, which is purchases and payments, identity and credentials and consent, physical acts and acts in T's own relationships, taste and appetite T has reserved, choices whose content is T's judgment, and anything requiring a human to be answerable. Rejected: tagging by 'needs approval' (marks everything), a frontmatter classifier (the unit classified is the step, and a classifier cannot address a step), a graded scale (invites argument where the useful question is binary), and marking the AI-doable inverse (the estate marks the exception, and the exception is the smaller set). Grey band rule: tag the step if any part of it is human-only and say in the step what the agent does up to that line — a tag is a boundary marker, not an abdication. Binds chart and phase outputs from 2026-08-28 forward, does not rewrite sealed roadmaps, does bind the unmerged idea-0004 roadmap; reopens if agent capability swallows a tagged category, if the tag stops discriminating by appearing nearly everywhere or nowhere, or if a tagged step is ever completed without T's hands. It governs the form of roadmaps and not their content, and it does not touch idea-0004's two still-owed decisions, which remain open.

### state/0002 · 2026-08-26 · session-verb: none · wrote outside the record: reference/, docs/adr/0017-okf-documentation.md
The "OKF" reference that has ridden as an open question since ADR 0008 is answered: it is Google Cloud's Open Knowledge Format (v0.2), not an OpenAI format. T pointed at the spec; it is now vendored, and the estate's documentation adopted it (ADR 0017): — A root reference/ bundle — the spec plus one OKF concept per verb (17), office (13), and artifact type (10), and core concepts for the law, the record model, scoring, lenses, shapes, playbooks, falsifiers, and the estate itself. Every concept's sources names the governing file; system/ wins where they disagree. — OKF frontmatter on all prose …

### state/0003 · 2026-08-26 · session-verb: none · wrote outside the record: docs/adr/0018-findings-speak-okf.md
T asked whether research should drop Findings into reference/ as OKF documents. Answered and sealed as ADR 0018: Findings speak OKF but live in the record — the artifact extends record frontmatter with the OKF families (sources: with credibility signals as the citations, per-claim footnotes, actor-convention generated:, honest stale_after:), stays in artifacts/ where the machinery consumes it, and a finding with cross-record value is promoted to reference/ by operator selection, citing the artifact as source. Relocation was rejected: it would hide Findings from the inputs chains and gap …

### state/0004 · 2026-08-26 · session-verb: none · wrote outside the record: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/adr/0019-claude-md-imports-agents-md.md, README.md, docs/adr/README.md
T proposed renaming or duplicating AGENTS.md as CLAUDE.md "to make sure that Claude Code 100% reads it." Both were declined in favour of the harness's own mechanism: CLAUDE.md is now a single @AGENTS.md import, expanded into context at session start, plus a short Claude-Code-specific note. Sealed as ADR 0019.

The defect was real and observed in this very session: CLAUDE.md was injected at startup and AGENTS.md was not, so the standing identity arrived only because the main session elected to spend a tool call on ADR 0015's prose pointer. That closed F-3 by compliance; the import closes it by …

### state/0005 · 2026-08-27 · session-verb: none · wrote outside the record: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/adr/0019-claude-md-imports-agents-md.md, docs/adr/0017-okf-documentation.md, docs/adr/README.md
T removed the OKF frontmatter from CLAUDE.md, then from AGENTS.md, and pointed at the OKF announcement to settle why. The blog is decisive: OKF is a bundle format for concepts — directories of markdown whose file paths form each concept's identity, cross-linked into a graph, consumed by catalogs, search, and agents browsing the bundle. That is reference/, exactly.

A memory file is not a concept and has no bundle. The harness reads it by injecting it verbatim at session start, so the frontmatter was never conformance — it was OKF's shape applied outside the format's scope, costing tokens …

========================================================================
# idea-0003: The Starvu agency site
========================================================================

status: active · appetite: 1 (placeholder) · created: 2026-08-27 · state-head: state/0012.md · seed: exports/0003-starvu-agency-site-seed.md
relates (note, not an edge): no edges drawn; `relate` is The Cartographer's, and it has not run

## Artifacts — the agents' track

### 0001 · Spark · "The Starvu agency site"
capture · The Gardener · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [] · challenged: false
A website for a friend's new talent-management business promoting models and OnlyFans creators — must feel ✨expensive✨, not dark or neon or sleazy — with a supplied black-and-gold flyer and logo that pull the other way.

### 0002 · Spark · "The North Star"
capture · The Gardener · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0001] · challenged: false
T declares the North Star: adult film creators arrive, feel confident Starvu can advise and support them growing their platform accounts, learn the services — chatting, advising, content protection — and book a 1:1 consultation on the calendar.

### 0003 · Findings · "The three reference sites, observed"
research · The Factor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0001, 0002] · challenged: false · stale_after: 2026-11-27
The three reference sites, observed 2026-08-27: all three run an apply-to-qualify funnel whose prize is a free strategy call, none shows an age gate or a non-affiliation statement, and the visual register question cannot be answered from text alone — no rendered pixels were seen.

### 0004 · Findings · "Still blind, and I have to say so first"
research · The Factor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0003, 0002] · challenged: false · stale_after: 2026-11-27
Re-dispatch on the visual question: the browser named in The Factor's definition was NOT PRESENT in this runtime, so the visual register is still unobserved and the three judgments are still unanswerable. What the second pass did add: Foxy's homepage imagery is substantially AI-generated Freepik stock, Eros is a Webflow build, and AT Agency remains wholly unreachable.

### 0005 · Findings · "What the instrument actually turned out to be"
research · The Factor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0004, 0002] · challenged: false · stale_after: 2026-11-27
The browser arrived. All three sites rendered — AT Agency for the first time in four passes — and their palettes and typography were read from computed style. Eros is the dark/neon one (#050505 + #EC1194 + film grain). Foxy is the light editorial one (#FFFFFF + #0D1129 + Playfair Display). AT Agency is black + electric blue tech-SaaS. My standing inference about Foxy is half-overturned: its surface is the most expensive of the three, its quantity is the least. Screenshots still failed, so no photograph was seen.

### 0006 · Findings · "The instrument, once, and then not again"
research · The Factor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0005, 0002] · challenged: false · stale_after: 2026-11-27
A functional inventory of the three reference sites, gathered for a builder. All three run an earnings calculator or none-of-the-above (two of three do — the packet's premise that Foxy alone has one is wrong). Foxy is a static Netlify site with zero fetch() on its homepage, a Calendly exposed before any form, a lead-magnet second funnel, and a fake-live dashboard plus hardcoded social-proof toasts; its 'Ask us anything' chat input has no JavaScript behind it at all. Eros is Webflow with a three-step quiz form, no calendar anywhere, and an unused Webflow Memberships login stack sitting unlinked in its sitemap. AT is a React SPA with a real backend (/api/apply, /api/track), a referral program with session-tracked attribution, and the smallest claimed numbers in the set (4+ years, 12+ creators). No age gate on any route of any site.

### 0007 · Findings · "Foxy's booking page, taken apart"
research · The Factor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0006, 0005] · challenged: false · stale_after: 2026-09-30
Foxy's booking page taken apart as an experience. /book-a-call is a 404 — the nav label points at /contact. The page is 5 sections and 5.94 desktop screens against the homepage's 17 and 22.3: the same company choosing brevity, which is the finding. The 'fancy' is four cheap choices — italic Playfair Display at weight 500 for every display line, a four-colour palette with a single accent, exactly two shadow tokens, and a uniform 6rem section rhythm. The calendar is a stock Calendly embed themed by one query parameter and one 24px-radius overflow-hidden wrapper; there is no custom UI. There are no scroll reveals and no entrance animation anywhere. The only custom easing on the page is spent on the post-submit success modal. On mobile that same rounded wrapper clips 17px off the right edge of the calendar. Reduced-motion covers one floating button and nothing else.

### 0008 · Framing · "The ground under the Starvu site"
frame · The Gardener · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0001, 0002, 0006, 0007] · challenged: false
The ground under the Starvu site: two horizons that must not collapse into each other — a long-term web presence for the business, and an immediate landing page whose whole job is to carry a creator from arrival to a booked 1:1. The problem underneath is a proof floor: Starvu must earn a stranger's professional trust on day one with zero track record, in a category whose trust furniture is substantially manufactured, using a mark that points at the register its own brief rejects. Names what is in and out of scope for each horizon, the four constraint sets (T's, the friend's, the category's, compliance), eight assumptions the record is running on, the three live decisions the record has surfaced and not taken, and the largest unnamed hole: nothing anywhere says how a creator arrives.

### 0009 · Framing · "The ground under the Starvu site, after attack"
challenge · The Advocate · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0008] · challenged: true
The central claim breaks in half: Starvu cannot make performance claims — that part holds — but 'therefore the site must substitute confidence for a track record' does not follow, and the 'proof floor' it rests on is one hardcoded string in a competitor's JavaScript bundle, which the record's own Findings class as 'not evidence of anything true.' Three attacks drew blood: the brevity argument imports the economy of a page that inherits its persuasion from a 22-screen homepage upstream, and so is condemned by the Framing's own no-stub constraint; 'an audience equipped to check' is asserted against a record in which the checking demonstrably failed, while the two references that manufacture proof are the two working businesses; and the confidence claim is not merely unfalsified but unfalsifiable by construction of the near horizon, because nothing in it will generate a signal that could distinguish success from failure. The replacement ground: Starvu substitutes verifiability for track record, not confidence — it can be the most checkable business in the reference set on identity, entity, and compliance, all of which are real, cheap, and already in inventory. The distribution hole reorders the record: whether traffic is warm or cold decides whether the central claim applies at all, and that is one conversation, not a dispatch. Held under attack: the two-horizon separation, the compliance-in-scope argument, the funnel-consecutiveness reading, the three live decisions, and the hole itself.

### 0010 · Horizon · "The Starvu page, six months in"
envision · The Architect · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0009] · challenged: false · horizon: falsifiable
Six months out, the Starvu landing page is a single expensive-looking instrument that does one thing no competitor's site does: it discloses the whole business — the entity, the man, the agreement you will be asked to sign, the eligibility rules, the split, the 90-day exit — and then books fifteen minutes with him against real availability. The design problem T handed over ('as many meaningful features as possible' against 'nothing may be a stub') is resolved by a distinction the reference set makes visible: every feature Foxy and AT built is an ASSERTION machine that needs a business behind it to be true, and every one of them is therefore hollow; a DISCLOSURE instrument needs only a fact in front of it, and Starvu is rich in facts and poor in track record. That inverts the constraint from a budget into a generator — the page can be feature-dense precisely because its features are made of things already true. Twelve features are real on day one, six become real once one cheap thing lands (photo permission, the first month's own numbers, a set split, three creators willing to say a sentence), and seven are named as forbidden until the business is older, with the earnings calculator refused outright and permanently in the generator form the category uses. The page branches on warm-versus-cold traffic only in months four to six and only in what gets added around the booking, not in what the page is. Falsifier set inherited from 0009 §4 and extended with five of my own, the sharpest being: if twenty creators come off calls and not one of them mentions the terms, the entity, or the 90-day trial unprompted, the whole feature spine is wrong.

### 0011 · Horizon · "The Starvu page, six months in — and the machinery behind it"
explore · The Forager · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0010] · challenged: false · horizon: falsifiable
The answer to T's three-surface question is uneven on purpose: internal tooling is where almost all the value is and the honesty test does not bind it at all; visitor-facing AI is almost entirely refused and gets one narrow exception; and the creator portal is earned much earlier than 0010 said, because 0010 sorted it by category evidence rather than by its own test. The exploration's central find is that 'portal' names two different objects that share a word — a login link on a public page with nothing behind it is Eros's exact defect and stays refused forever, while a client portal holding a signed creator's own agreement, her verification status, her weekly numbers and her takedown log is a DISCLOSURE INSTRUMENT with an audience of one, and it becomes honest the day the second creator signs. The resolution that satisfies both 0010 and T at once: the portal is real, and the public site never links to it. Fifteen internal candidates are developed, of which two cost an afternoon each and change what the page can honestly say — a call-notes capture that funds the real FAQ and the sharpest inherited falsifier, and a claims ledger that makes the no-stub audit a build step rather than a habit. Six hazards bite hard and one of them is new to the record and structural: mainstream model providers prohibit adult sexual content generation, so the chat-drafting tool everyone reaches for first is not an afternoon, it is a different infrastructure decision — and OnlyFans's automation ban lands on the creator's account, not Starvu's, which makes it a fiduciary question rather than a compliance one. Five new falsifiers, the sharpest being the tooling bet: hand the friend the notes capture for two weeks, and if it is empty at week two, build nothing else internal.

### 0012 · Trajectory · "The route from here to the Starvu page at month six"
chart · The Surveyor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0011] · challenged: false · trajectory: actionable
The route is not a page being built forward — it is a short errand that gates months, then a launch, then a long quiet middle in which almost nothing visible happens while four fuses burn, and then two harvests where the page grows in bursts as facts arrive. The sequencing principle that falls out of the Forager's supply-line finding is the one thing this artifact adds: every page feature on the 'real soon' tier is downstream of a tool that must be BUILT and then RUN IDLE for a ripening period, so build order is governed by fuse length, not by build cost — light the long fuses first, even the cheap ones. That re-ranks one item off the Forager's list: the response-time meter is an afternoon with a one-month fuse and sits at position 6, which means it delivers its number a month later than it needs to; it belongs beside the notes capture in the same week. Six legs, five checkpoints placed where they actually fall rather than listed at the end, and each checkpoint carries the re-route it triggers. Three findings the Horizon did not have about itself: falsifier 10 failing DISARMS falsifier 5, because the notes capture is the only instrument that runs the disclosure bet, so the two-week tooling test needs a fallback that moves the question off the friend's Tuesday and onto the booking flow; falsifier 10 as written ('build nothing else internal') over-reaches, because half the tools observe behaviour already happening and require no habit at all; and gating the calendar lengthens the fuse on the traffic checkpoint, which is a cost of the Chancellor's decision 2 that has not been weighed against it. The first actionable step is a text message that can be sent Monday morning, and it is the cheapest thing on the route by two orders of magnitude.

### 0013 · Phase · "Phase 1 — The errand"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0012] · challenged: false
Delivers nine written answers — six from the friend, two decisions of T's, and one pre-registered number — and it starts now, on a Monday morning, waiting on nothing. This is Leg 0 decomposed, and the decomposition added three items the Trajectory could not have: the careers tab arriving from T after the chart was drawn puts two questions on the same message (who reads that inbox, and within what window) and one on the friend's lawyer (does the Talent Management Agreement already name who may speak as a creator), and that third one has acquired a deadline it did not have before — the first chatter hire. Cost: an afternoon, most of which is waiting for a reply. Done looks like nine answers in one file, dated, plus a vendor chosen and identity documents no longer arriving over WhatsApp. No checkpoint sits here, but the record's earliest falsifier can fire here — if the friend will not publish the agreement, features 1 and 2 do not ship, the clause finder leaves the route, and the correct response is to return to envision rather than to build the page anyway.

### 0014 · Phase · "Phase 2 — Ship v1, instrumented"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0012] · challenged: false
Delivers the live page — the twelve day-one features minus whatever Phase 1 struck out, the careers tab brought under the no-stub rule, and fifteen minutes of instrumentation that is the denominator for everything the record will later claim to know — and it starts when the v1 design returns from flight, which for most of its content is already. Two publication answers from Phase 1 gate features 1 and 2 and nothing else gates anything. Cost: weeks, and it is the only Phase on the route measured in weeks. Done looks like a page where every affordance has a machine behind it, the per-channel tags emit, and 'How did you hear about Starvu?' is asked of creators on a form that no applicant ever sees. Decisions 1, 2 and 3 all bite here and nowhere else on the route; the careers tab lands here as a second funnel that must share the disclosure furniture and must not share the instrumentation, because a shared attribution field puts two populations into the one field Checkpoint C reads.

### 0015 · Phase · "Phase 3 — Light the fuses"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0012] · challenged: false
Delivers three tools — the call-notes capture, the response-time meter and the claims ledger — whose entire purpose is to start burning, and it starts as soon as the friend takes his next call, which means item 1 of it does not wait for the page to ship and should be handed over during Phase 2 rather than after it. That is the decomposition's sharpest reordering: the Trajectory put this leg 'the same week as launch or the week after,' but the notes capture's fuse is measured in calls and he is already taking calls, so by the route's own rule — fuse length is not buyable back — every call taken before the notebook exists is a call spent. Cost: three afternoons, spread over two weeks, and the meter's afternoon is gated on Phase 1's answer about whether support exports. Checkpoint A sits at the end of this Phase, two weeks after the capture is handed over, and it is the cheapest and sharpest checkpoint on the route: if the notebook is empty, the class of tools that asks the friend to change his Tuesday is dead, the class that merely watches survives, and the pre-committed fallback moves 'what made you book?' onto the booking confirmation so that the record does not lose its ability to check its own central claim.

### 0016 · Phase · "Phase 4 — The quiet month"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0012] · challenged: false
Delivers two weekend builds — the manual-assist takedown assistant and the onboarding-and-verification tracker — and, more importantly, delivers a month of elapsed operating in which the page does not change at all, and it starts the moment Checkpoint A resolves. The correct amount of visible page progress in this Phase is zero, and that is the single hardest thing about it: a phased plan is exactly where a quiet month gets accidentally filled with page work, and filling it delivers four of the six middle-tier features a month late because the fuses were never left to burn. Cost: two weekends inside a month of nothing. Two checkpoints close it — Checkpoint B, one month of takedown work, which can remove content protection from the services block and therefore shrink the page; and Checkpoint F, arriving from T with the careers tab, which asks whether anyone answered the applications and can shrink the page the same way. Checkpoint A governs whether the tracker gets built at all, because the tracker asks the friend for records and is therefore in the class the tooling bet can kill.

### 0017 · Phase · "Phase 5 — First harvest"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0012] · challenged: false
Delivers the page growing, in bursts, one row at a time as each fuse burns down — photographs of real creators, Starvu's own numbers, the median response time, the real FAQ, the published split, one creator's sentence, a services page written from a delivered week, the clause finder, and a content-protection log with real numbers — and it starts not on a single trigger but on whichever fuse burns down first, which is most likely the photographs, because they have no fuse at all. Cost: an afternoon per row, spread across weeks, and no row waits for another. One hard gate is promoted from a note: the one-hour unpublish path must exist before the first creator photograph ships, because publishing a real face is irreversible and permission granted in month two may be regretted in month twelve. Checkpoint D sits here — twenty calls, the disclosure bet — and it is the only checkpoint on the route that changes the destination rather than the path, sending the record back to envision with whatever the twenty creators actually said, the supply line intact. The careers tab contributes one conditional row of its own: the flyer's promise of a team that answers to you becomes evidenced the day a role is actually filled, and not one day earlier.

### 0018 · Phase · "Phase 6 — The portal, on a spur"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0012] · challenged: false
Delivers a client portal holding a signed creator's own agreement, her verification status, her 90-day clock and her weekly numbers — a disclosure instrument with an audience of one — and it starts on the second signed creator plus one deliverable that repeats, which could plausibly be month two or three rather than a far horizon. This Phase is a spur and not trunk: if it never happens, nothing else on the route changes, because the public page never links to it in any branch. Cost: one weekend for the portal and one weekend for the weekly numbers pack that gives the door something to hold, and the numbers pack is in the class Checkpoint A can kill because it asks the friend for records. The Chancellor's 0010-versus-0011 tension lands here and only here, and it must be resolved before the weekend is spent rather than before Phase 5, because the breach-minimising design rules — no legal names, no documents, no warehoused earnings, magic-link auth, expiring URLs — are the design and do not retrofit onto a built portal. Its own checkpoint: if signed creators log in once and never return within thirty days, the portal is a worse WhatsApp and the re-route is delivery over WhatsApp with the portal demoted to an archive nobody has to visit.

### 0019 · Phase · "Phase 7 — Down, or out"
phase · The Surveyor · 2026-08-27 · inputs: [0012] · challenged: false
Delivers months four to six of page work in exactly one of two directions — depth if traffic is warm, or one acquisition instrument if it is cold — and it starts when Checkpoint C fires at roughly twenty bookings, which is a volume trigger rather than a calendar one and may arrive before or after the harvest. The page is the same page in both branches; only what gets added around the booking differs, which is why the branch was safe to defer for six months and why nothing before this Phase needed the answer. Cost: the remaining months, and in the warm branch that cost is deliberately close to zero because the honest warm answer is that no acquisition surface gets built at all. Checkpoint C is unreadable if Phase 2's fifteen minutes of instrumentation were cut, and the honest response to that is to record the fork as permanently unsettled rather than to read the field anyway. Checkpoint E closes the route at month six: walk the page, and if any affordance has been quietly disabled, unlinked or drifted out of true, the discipline failed — which is a ten-minute walk that will be skipped unless the claims ledger shipped in Phase 3, in which case it is a build step that has been failing loudly since the day the drift started.

### state/0011 · 2026-08-27 · session-verb: phase · recorded: 0013, 0014, 0015, 0016, 0017, 0018, 0019
